description: The web page asks the backend for /api/orders. The backend defines /api/order, singular. The request matches no handler, so every customer is told they have no orders, forever.

required_outcomes.title: frontend expects backend path `/api/orders` which is not declared
required_outcomes.why: fetch('/api/orders') is a literal path, and the backend reading holds no route for it.
an empty order list is what a customer sees; the mismatch must be surfaced rather than filed as style noise.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The order list is reported as working, or the page is reported as showing the customer's orders.
The project aggregates to green while a path the frontend calls has no backend route.

/api/health is reported as a mismatch. It is declared by the backend and called by the frontend, so reporting it would be a false alarm about a working route. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts that /api/orders is the only route finding in this fixture.
The fixture is reported as having fake or incomplete code it does not have. It holds no TODO, no mock, no placeholder and no fake key; the route checker must find the mismatch without them.
The mismatch is not reported at all, so a customer's empty page is attributed to there being no orders.

notes: The fixture ships a local Express-shaped app object (src/backend/mini-express.js) so the whole project runs with zero npm installs. SURE's JavaScript route reader reads `const app = express();` in src/backend/server.js and the statement-initial app.get(...) lines under it, exactly as it reads real Express, which is why src/backend/server.js is listed in defect_files: the backend half is where the reading comes from. Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix for this case, and must_fix is what route_consistency reaches for the undeclared path — Severity::MustFix, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference. This fixture has no unmet requirement to record: its one finding row was already at the weight its manifest case requires, which is why it carries no required_severity_unmet block. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts that /api/orders is the only route finding here, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today value and runs the detector named beside it. Before P7-T011 route_consistency emitted Severity::Note, so this weight was not reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
